MEDICAL ONCOLOGY PROGRESS NOTE

Patient: Evelyn Carter
Date of birth: March 12, 1948
MRN: MRN-104582
Date of service: January 15, 2024
Facility: Northstar Cancer Center, 4100 Meridian Avenue, Austin, Texas 78704
Treating clinician: Maya Patel, MD
Study: SITE-CAN-0001

REASON FOR VISIT
Follow-up before cycle 2 of adjuvant FOLFOX for stage IIIA sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma.

INTERVAL HISTORY
Ms. Carter is a 75-year-old retired librarian who returns with her daughter, Lillian Carter. She tolerated the first infusion on January 2, 2024 with three days of grade 1 nausea, cold sensitivity, and mild fatigue. She used ondansetron twice and did not vomit. Appetite and weight are stable. Bowel movements occur once daily without blood or melena. She denies fever, dyspnea, chest pain, focal weakness, or persistent neuropathy. She reports mild tenderness over the right chest port but no erythema or drainage. She can be reached at 512-555-0148 or evelyn.carter@example.test. Her home address is 1842 Juniper Hollow Road, Austin, TX 78704.

ONCOLOGY HISTORY
Screening colonoscopy on September 18, 2023 found an obstructing sigmoid mass. Biopsy showed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with intact mismatch-repair proteins. CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis on September 25, 2023 showed no distant metastases. Dr. Aaron Kim performed robotic sigmoid colectomy on October 12, 2023. Pathology was pT3N1a with one of twenty-two nodes involved and negative margins. A port with serial number 4381-2204 was placed December 21, 2023.

MEDICATIONS
Oxaliplatin, leucovorin, and fluorouracil per protocol; ondansetron 8 mg as needed; lisinopril 10 mg daily; acetaminophen as needed. No known drug allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Otherwise negative for mouth sores, rash, urinary symptoms, falls, bleeding, or new pain.

EXAMINATION
Temperature 36.8 C, blood pressure 132/74, pulse 78, oxygen saturation 98 percent, weight 68.4 kg. She is alert and in no distress. Oral mucosa is moist without ulceration. No cervical adenopathy. Lungs are clear. Heart rhythm is regular. Abdomen is soft and nontender; surgical incisions are healed. Port site is clean. No edema. Sensation is intact in hands and feet.

DATA
WBC 5.8, ANC 3.4, hemoglobin 11.7, platelets 214, creatinine 0.82, bilirubin 0.6, AST 24, ALT 21. CEA was 2.1 on January 12, 2024.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Stage IIIA sigmoid colon cancer: laboratory values and performance status are adequate. Proceed with cycle 2 FOLFOX today without dose reduction. Planned duration is six months.
2. Chemotherapy nausea: continue dexamethasone and ondansetron; call if oral intake falls.
3. Cold sensitivity: reviewed avoidance of cold liquids for five days after oxaliplatin.
4. Port discomfort: no evidence of infection; monitor.
5. Surveillance: repeat CEA in three months and CT after completion of therapy.

Ms. Carter and Lillian Carter understood the plan. Written instructions were sent through the Northstar portal. Return February 5, 2024 before cycle 3. Note signed electronically by Maya Patel, MD on January 15, 2024.

MEDICAL ONCOLOGY PROGRESS NOTE

Patient: Evelyn Carter
DOB: 03/12/1948
Medical record number: MRN-104582
Encounter date: February 5, 2024
Location: Northstar Cancer Center, Austin clinic
Oncologist: Dr. Maya Patel

CHIEF CONCERN
Toxicity assessment before cycle 3 FOLFOX.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn Carter completed cycle 2 on January 15, 2024. Nausea was controlled, but she developed tingling in the fingertips when touching refrigerated food and transient throat discomfort with cold water. Symptoms resolved by day 8 and do not interfere with buttons, handwriting, or walking. She had two loose stools on January 20 and then returned to baseline. There has been no fever, mouth ulcer, rectal bleeding, or abdominal pain. She walks approximately one mile daily. Her daughter Lillian drove her from 1842 Juniper Hollow Road. The after-hours team confirmed her callback number as 512-555-0148.

CANCER SUMMARY
Sigmoid adenocarcinoma diagnosed September 18, 2023; robotic colectomy by Aaron Kim, MD on October 12, 2023; pT3N1a, margins negative, MMR proficient. Adjuvant therapy began January 2, 2024. No clinical or radiographic evidence of recurrent disease.

CURRENT THERAPY AND MEDICATION REVIEW
Modified FOLFOX every fourteen days. Home medicines include lisinopril, vitamin D, ondansetron, and prochlorperazine. Medication reconciliation was completed with Northstar pharmacist Jenna Woods. No allergies were reported.

PHYSICAL EXAM
ECOG performance status 0. Temperature 36.7 C, pulse 82, respirations 16, blood pressure 128/70, weight 67.9 kg. Well appearing and fully oriented. No oral lesions. Port over the right chest is intact. Lungs clear bilaterally. Regular heart sounds. Abdomen soft without mass, guarding, or ascites. No lower-extremity edema. Strength and light-touch sensation are normal.

LABORATORY REVIEW
WBC 4.6, ANC 2.5, hemoglobin 11.2, platelets 176, sodium 139, potassium 4.1, creatinine 0.79, albumin 3.9, bilirubin 0.5, AST 26, ALT 23. Values meet treatment parameters.

IMPRESSION
Stage IIIA colon adenocarcinoma on curative-intent adjuvant chemotherapy. Expected grade 1 cold-triggered neuropathy without persistent deficit. Mild chemotherapy-associated anemia.

PLAN
Proceed with cycle 3 at current doses. Continue standard antiemetic prophylaxis. The patient should report neuropathy lasting between cycles, inability to maintain hydration, temperature of 100.4 F or higher, or diarrhea more than four times daily. Arrange surgical follow-up with Dr. Aaron Kim on March 1, 2024. Next oncology assessment is February 19, 2024. Surveillance colonoscopy is due in October 2024.

Evelyn Carter agrees with the plan and had all questions answered. Note completed by Maya Patel, MD, Northstar Cancer Center, on February 5, 2024.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: Evelyn Carter
Date of birth: 03/12/1948
MRN: MRN-104582
Admission date: March 8, 2024
Discharge date: March 12, 2024
Attending physician: Olivia Chen, MD
Discharging facility: Northstar Cancer Center, 4100 Meridian Avenue, Austin, TX 78704

PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS
Neutropenic fever during adjuvant FOLFOX for stage IIIA sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma.

SECONDARY DIAGNOSES
Chemotherapy-associated pancytopenia, dehydration, oral mucositis, essential hypertension, and history of sigmoid colectomy.

HOSPITAL COURSE
Evelyn Carter presented to the Northstar emergency department on March 8, 2024 after reporting a temperature of 101.3 F to the oncology triage line at 512-555-0199. Initial ANC was 0.3, blood pressure 108/62, lactate 1.4, and creatinine 1.08 compared with a baseline of 0.8. Examination showed shallow oral ulcers without respiratory, abdominal, urinary, or port-site findings. Blood cultures were obtained from the port and periphery. Urine culture and chest radiograph were negative. She received intravenous cefepime, fluids, and filgrastim. Vancomycin was stopped after forty-eight hours because cultures remained negative and the port appeared normal. Fever resolved on March 9. ANC recovered to 1.6 on March 11 and 3.2 on March 12. Oral intake improved with saline rinses and topical lidocaine. No organism was identified.

Oncology consultant Maya Patel, MD recommended delaying cycle 6 and adding pegfilgrastim to future cycles. The patient had no bleeding, thrombosis, hypoxia, delirium, or fall. Lillian Carter participated in bedside teaching. Case manager Robert Ellis confirmed transportation to the home at 1842 Juniper Hollow Road, Austin, Texas 78704.

PROCEDURES AND RESULTS
No invasive procedure was required. Chest radiograph dated March 8 showed no acute infiltrate. Final blood cultures had no growth at five days. Discharge laboratory results were WBC 5.1, ANC 3.2, hemoglobin 9.8, platelets 112, sodium 140, potassium 3.8, creatinine 0.81, AST 19, ALT 17, and bilirubin 0.4.

DISCHARGE EXAM
Afebrile, pulse 76, blood pressure 124/68, oxygen saturation 98 percent on room air. Alert and ambulatory. Mucositis is improving. Port site is clean. Lungs clear, abdomen soft, and no edema.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS
Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily, ondansetron 8 mg every eight hours as needed, prochlorperazine 10 mg every six hours as needed, and saline mouth rinses. Start levofloxacin 500 mg daily through March 14, 2024. Chemotherapy remains on hold until oncology reassessment.

FOLLOW-UP
Appointment with Maya Patel, MD at Northstar Cancer Center on March 18, 2024 at 9:20 AM. CBC will be drawn before the visit. Call 512-555-0148 for routine scheduling or 512-555-0199 for fever, shaking chills, dyspnea, inability to drink, confusion, or bleeding. Discharge instructions were also sent to evelyn.carter@example.test.

CONDITION AND DISPOSITION
Stable for discharge home with family. Evelyn Carter demonstrated understanding of medications, infection precautions, and follow-up. Summary signed by Olivia Chen, MD on March 12, 2024.

GI MEDICAL ONCOLOGY PROGRESS NOTE

Patient: Marcus Lee
DOB: November 4, 1965
MRN: MRN-208731
Date: April 8, 2024
Clinic: Harborview Oncology Institute, 955 Harbor Loop, Houston, Texas 77030
Provider: Samuel Ortiz, MD

REASON FOR VISIT
New-patient treatment planning for borderline resectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

HISTORY
Mr. Lee is a 58-year-old civil engineer referred by Dr. Priya Shah. He developed painless jaundice and dark urine on March 2, 2024. CT at Gulf Coast Imaging on March 5 showed a 3.4 cm pancreatic-head mass with abutment of the superior mesenteric vein and no distant metastasis. ERCP performed March 7 placed a metal common-bile-duct stent, serial 7714-3098. Endoscopic ultrasound biopsy confirmed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Bilirubin has fallen from 12.8 to 1.6. He reports early satiety and a twelve-pound weight loss but remains active and independent. There is mild epigastric discomfort controlled with acetaminophen. No vomiting, fever, diarrhea, chest pain, or neuropathy.

Marcus Lee lives with spouse Andrew Lee at 77 Bayberry Court, Houston, TX 77025. Preferred phone is 713-555-0126 and email is marcus.lee@example.test. His insurance member identifier is HPI-5520-8831.

PAST HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and remote appendectomy. Family history includes ovarian cancer in his mother, Helen Lee, at age 64. He has never smoked and drinks alcohol rarely.

MEDICATIONS
Metformin extended release 1000 mg nightly, atorvastatin 20 mg nightly, pancreatic enzymes with meals, and acetaminophen as needed. No known drug allergies.

EXAM
ECOG 1. Blood pressure 118/72, pulse 84, temperature 36.6 C, weight 74.2 kg. Scleral icterus has nearly resolved. No adenopathy. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft with mild epigastric tenderness and no ascites. No edema.

LABS AND IMAGING
WBC 6.9, hemoglobin 12.4, platelets 286, creatinine 0.91, glucose 164, albumin 3.6, bilirubin 1.6, alkaline phosphatase 288, AST 48, ALT 61. CA 19-9 is 436. CT images were reviewed in multidisciplinary conference.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Borderline resectable pancreatic-head adenocarcinoma, cT2N0M0. Begin modified FOLFIRINOX on April 15, 2024 after port placement. Plan four months of systemic therapy followed by restaging and surgical review. Refer to genetic counseling given family history and arrange germline panel. Continue pancreatic enzymes and dietitian support. Monitor diabetes closely during dexamethasone exposure. Fever, recurrent jaundice, uncontrolled pain, or inability to eat requires immediate contact.

The risks of neuropathy, cytopenias, diarrhea, nausea, infection, and thrombosis were discussed. Marcus Lee and Andrew Lee provided informed agreement. Return April 29, 2024. Electronically signed by Samuel Ortiz, MD.

GI ONCOLOGY FOLLOW-UP

Name: Marcus Lee
Date of birth: 11/04/1965
Record: MRN-208731
Service date: April 29, 2024
Harborview Oncology Institute, Houston campus
Samuel Ortiz, MD

INTERVAL HISTORY
Marcus Lee returns before cycle 2 modified FOLFIRINOX for borderline resectable pancreatic cancer. Cycle 1 was administered April 15, 2024. He experienced fatigue for five days, two days of loose stool, and brief cold sensitivity. Loperamide controlled diarrhea. He did not have fever or vomiting. Appetite improved after dietitian counseling, and weight increased by 0.6 kg. Epigastric pain is now 1 of 10. Urine and stool color are normal. He reports no recurrent jaundice, port symptoms, dyspnea, calf pain, or focal weakness. Blood glucose rose to 240 after dexamethasone but returned below 160 with guidance from primary clinician Nina Wallace, DO.

ONCOLOGIC STATUS
Biopsy-proven pancreatic-head adenocarcinoma diagnosed March 7, 2024. Baseline CT showed venous abutment without arterial encasement or metastasis. Metal biliary stent remains in place. CA 19-9 decreased from 436 to 318. Germline testing was collected April 22 under accession GEN-942771; results are pending.

SOCIAL AND CONTACT INFORMATION
He continues working remotely from 77 Bayberry Court. Andrew Lee is the designated contact at 713-555-0177. Patient phone remains 713-555-0126.

EXAMINATION
ECOG 1. Temperature 36.5 C, blood pressure 121/69, pulse 80, weight 74.8 kg. No jaundice or oral ulcers. Port is well healed. Lungs clear, regular cardiac rhythm, abdomen nontender, no ascites or edema, and no persistent sensory deficit.

LABORATORY DATA
WBC 5.2, ANC 2.9, hemoglobin 11.8, platelets 192, creatinine 0.86, bilirubin 0.9, alkaline phosphatase 176, AST 31, ALT 39, magnesium 1.9.

ASSESSMENT
Treatment is tolerated with manageable grade 1 gastrointestinal toxicity and transient neuropathy. Liver tests continue to improve after biliary decompression. No evidence of cholangitis.

PLAN
Proceed with cycle 2 at full planned doses. Reduce post-treatment dexamethasone to two days because of hyperglycemia. Continue pancreatic enzymes, hydration, and loperamide as needed. Schedule CT pancreas protocol after cycle 4 on June 6, 2024 and surgical consultation with Rebecca Huang, MD on June 10. The patient should call Harborview at 713-555-0100 for fever, jaundice, persistent diarrhea, or uncontrolled pain.

Marcus Lee verbalized understanding. Note signed by Samuel Ortiz, MD on April 29, 2024.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: Marcus Lee
DOB: 11/04/1965
MRN: MRN-208731
Admission: May 14, 2024
Discharge: May 18, 2024
Facility: Harborview Oncology Institute, 955 Harbor Loop, Houston, TX 77030
Attending: Rebecca Huang, MD

ADMISSION DIAGNOSIS
Acute cholangitis caused by occlusion of a biliary stent in a patient receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy for pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES
Resolved cholangitis and sepsis without shock; pancreatic-head adenocarcinoma; chemotherapy-associated anemia; type 2 diabetes; and protein-calorie malnutrition.

PRESENTATION
Marcus Lee came to the emergency department on May 14 with fever to 102.1 F, rigors, right-upper-quadrant pain, and recurrent jaundice. Spouse Andrew Lee called 713-555-0100 before arrival. Laboratory testing showed WBC 14.8, bilirubin 5.7, alkaline phosphatase 512, lactate 2.3, and creatinine 1.02. CT demonstrated biliary dilation above the existing metal stent with no new metastasis.

HOSPITAL COURSE
Blood cultures grew Escherichia coli susceptible to ceftriaxone. Piperacillin-tazobactam was started on admission. Gastroenterologist Leah Morgan, MD performed ERCP on May 15, removed debris, and placed a plastic stent through the prior metal stent. Procedure identifier was ERCP-2024-0515-77. Bilirubin improved to 1.4 by discharge. Fever and abdominal pain resolved, oral intake improved, and repeat cultures were negative. Chemotherapy was held. Endocrinology managed transient hyperglycemia with correction insulin. Dietitian Carla Nguyen recommended high-protein meals and pancreatic enzymes with every meal.

No respiratory failure, hypotension requiring vasopressors, bleeding, or intensive-care transfer occurred. The right chest port remained uninfected. Andrew Lee received return-precaution teaching.

DISCHARGE EXAM AND DATA
Temperature 36.8 C, blood pressure 116/66, pulse 74, oxygen saturation 97 percent. Mild residual scleral icterus, clear lungs, regular heart rhythm, soft nontender abdomen, and no edema. WBC 6.4, hemoglobin 10.6, platelets 168, creatinine 0.84, bilirubin 1.4, AST 42, ALT 55.

MEDICATIONS
Start ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily through May 24, 2024. Continue pancreatic enzymes, metformin when eating normally, atorvastatin, ondansetron as needed, and acetaminophen as needed. Do not restart chemotherapy until cleared by oncology.

FOLLOW-UP
Samuel Ortiz, MD on May 22, 2024 at Harborview Oncology Institute. Repeat CBC and comprehensive metabolic panel before the visit. Repeat ERCP for stent exchange is scheduled July 10, 2024. Call 713-555-0100 for fever, jaundice, vomiting, confusion, or worsening pain. Written instructions were sent to marcus.lee@example.test.

DISPOSITION
Discharged home to 77 Bayberry Court with Andrew Lee in stable condition. Marcus Lee understood the medication and follow-up plan. Summary signed by Rebecca Huang, MD on May 18, 2024.

BREAST MEDICAL ONCOLOGY PROGRESS NOTE

Patient: Sofia Ramirez
Date of birth: July 22, 1979
MRN: MRN-315904
Date of service: June 3, 2024
Facility: Redwood Regional Medical Center, 220 Redwood Plaza, San Antonio, Texas 78229
Clinician: Hannah Green, MD

REASON FOR VISIT
Evaluation before week 5 neoadjuvant paclitaxel, carboplatin, and pembrolizumab for stage IIB triple-negative breast cancer.

INTERVAL HISTORY
Sofia Ramirez is a 44-year-old high-school counselor who reports moderate fatigue beginning two days after treatment and resolving by the weekend. She has mild tingling in both toes but no gait change or hand symptoms. Nausea is controlled with prochlorperazine. She denies fever, cough, diarrhea, rash, dyspnea, chest pain, or new breast pain. The left breast mass feels smaller. She continues to work four days per week. Her sister, Elena Ramirez, accompanies her. Contact information is 210-555-0164 and sofia.ramirez@example.test. She resides at 908 Mission Laurel Drive, San Antonio, TX 78212.

DISEASE HISTORY
Diagnostic mammogram on April 4, 2024 identified a 3.1 cm left upper-outer-quadrant mass and abnormal axillary node. Biopsies on April 9 showed grade 3 invasive ductal carcinoma, ER negative, PR negative, HER2 0, and metastatic carcinoma in the node. PET-CT on April 18 showed no distant disease. Clinical stage is cT2N1M0. Germline panel was negative. Baseline echocardiogram ejection fraction was 63 percent.

MEDICATIONS
Weekly paclitaxel and carboplatin with pembrolizumab every three weeks; levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; prochlorperazine as needed. Allergy to sulfonamide antibiotics causes rash.

EXAM
ECOG 0. Temperature 36.9 C, blood pressure 126/78, pulse 88, weight 61.3 kg. No oral lesions. No cervical adenopathy. Left breast mass measures approximately 1.8 cm; axillary node is less distinct. Port is intact. Lungs clear, heart regular, abdomen benign, no edema, and light touch is preserved.

LABS
WBC 3.9, ANC 2.1, hemoglobin 10.9, platelets 201, creatinine 0.71, bilirubin 0.4, AST 22, ALT 25, TSH 2.8, free T4 1.1.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Clinical response is evident and laboratory values meet treatment criteria. Proceed with week 5 paclitaxel and carboplatin. Pembrolizumab is due next week. Monitor grade 1 neuropathy and reduce paclitaxel if symptoms become persistent or affect function. Continue thyroid monitoring every six weeks. Breast MRI is planned after completion of the taxane phase. Surgical consultation with Melissa Grant, MD is scheduled August 19, 2024.

Sofia Ramirez was reminded to call 210-555-0105 for fever at or above 100.4 F, uncontrolled diarrhea, shortness of breath, or rapidly progressive rash. Note signed electronically by Hannah Green, MD on June 3, 2024.

BREAST ONCOLOGY FOLLOW-UP NOTE

Name: Sofia Ramirez
DOB: 07/22/1979
MRN: MRN-315904
Encounter date: June 24, 2024
Redwood Regional Medical Center, San Antonio
Hannah Green, MD

SUBJECTIVE
Sofia Ramirez presents before week 8 of neoadjuvant therapy. Since June 17 she has had increased fatigue and numbness limited to the distal toes. She can walk, drive, type, and work without limitation. She developed a faint nonpruritic rash on both forearms that improved with fragrance-free moisturizer. There is no blistering, facial swelling, fever, diarrhea, cough, or dyspnea. Appetite is fair and weight is stable. She reports complete resolution of the palpable left breast mass. She has not missed levothyroxine. Elena Ramirez remains available at 210-555-0182 if assistance is needed.

TREATMENT HISTORY
Paclitaxel and carboplatin began May 6, 2024. Pembrolizumab doses were given May 6, May 27, and June 17. No prior dose reductions. The patient is enrolled in registry SITE-CAN-0003. Infusion pump asset number is 6631-4402.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative except as described for fatigue, distal sensory symptoms, and improving rash. Specifically no headache, visual change, mouth sore, dysphagia, chest pain, palpitations, abdominal pain, urinary complaint, bleeding, or focal weakness.

OBJECTIVE
ECOG 1. Temperature 36.7 C, pulse 86, blood pressure 122/75, weight 60.9 kg. Alopecia present. Oral mucosa clear. No palpable cervical or supraclavicular nodes. No discrete left breast mass on examination and axillary fullness has improved. Port without tenderness. Lungs clear. Regular cardiac rhythm. Abdomen soft. Trace erythematous macules on forearms cover less than five percent of body surface. No edema. Decreased vibration at great toes, with normal gait.

LABORATORY RESULTS
WBC 2.8, ANC 1.4, hemoglobin 9.9, platelets 154, sodium 138, creatinine 0.69, AST 27, ALT 31, bilirubin 0.3, TSH 3.1.

ASSESSMENT
Stage IIB triple-negative left breast cancer with excellent clinical response. Grade 1 sensory neuropathy, grade 1 immune-related rash, and chemotherapy-associated anemia and neutropenia.

PLAN
Proceed with week 8 paclitaxel and carboplatin because ANC remains acceptable. Continue pembrolizumab on schedule. Begin triamcinolone 0.1 percent cream twice daily for recurrent rash and notify the clinic if rash spreads. Continue neuropathy monitoring. Repeat CBC on July 1. MRI breast is scheduled July 29, 2024. The next visit with Hannah Green, MD is July 15.

Sofia Ramirez understands the plan. A copy was sent through the Redwood portal to sofia.ramirez@example.test. Signed June 24, 2024.

INPATIENT DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: Sofia Ramirez
DOB: July 22, 1979
MRN: MRN-315904
Admitted: July 8, 2024
Discharged: July 11, 2024
Facility: Redwood Regional Medical Center, 220 Redwood Plaza, San Antonio, TX 78229
Attending hospitalist: Jonathan Price, MD

REASON FOR ADMISSION
Febrile neutropenia and symptomatic anemia during neoadjuvant treatment for triple-negative breast cancer.

CLINICAL COURSE
Sofia Ramirez presented with chills, oral temperature 101.8 F, heart rate 112, and profound fatigue five days after week 9 paclitaxel and carboplatin. Admission ANC was 0.2 and hemoglobin 7.4. Chest radiograph, urinalysis, respiratory viral panel, and examination of the port did not identify a source. Cefepime was started immediately after peripheral and port blood cultures. She received one unit of leukoreduced packed red blood cells on July 8 without reaction and filgrastim on July 9 and July 10. Cultures remained negative. She became afebrile within twenty-four hours, ANC recovered to 1.3, and hemoglobin stabilized at 9.1.

The oncology service, led by Hannah Green, MD, recommended omitting the next carboplatin dose and resuming treatment only after outpatient review. The mild forearm rash resolved without systemic steroids. There was no diarrhea, hypoxia, hypotension, bleeding, immune-mediated organ toxicity, or intensive-care requirement. Physical therapy confirmed independent mobility. Sister Elena Ramirez participated in discharge planning by telephone at 210-555-0182.

PERTINENT RESULTS
Discharge WBC 3.2, ANC 1.3, hemoglobin 9.1, platelets 98, creatinine 0.67, bilirubin 0.4, AST 20, ALT 22. Blood cultures had no growth at seventy-two hours. Chest radiograph on July 8 showed clear lungs and appropriate port position.

DISCHARGE EXAM
Temperature 36.6 C, blood pressure 119/72, pulse 79, oxygen saturation 99 percent. Awake and comfortable. No oral ulcer, rash, adenopathy, breast tenderness, pulmonary abnormality, abdominal tenderness, or edema. Port site clean.

MEDICATIONS AND INSTRUCTIONS
Continue levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, prochlorperazine as needed, and triamcinolone cream only if rash recurs. No outpatient antibiotic is required. Chemotherapy and pembrolizumab are held until oncology review. Avoid sick contacts, perform careful hand hygiene, and check temperature for recurrent chills.

FOLLOW-UP
CBC and visit with Hannah Green, MD on July 15, 2024 at 8:40 AM. Call 210-555-0105 or go to the emergency department for temperature at or above 100.4 F, dyspnea, confusion, bleeding, or inability to drink. Results and instructions were released to sofia.ramirez@example.test.

DISPOSITION
Stable, discharged home to 908 Mission Laurel Drive with Elena Ramirez. Sofia Ramirez repeated back the precautions correctly. Summary signed by Jonathan Price, MD on July 11, 2024.

THORACIC ONCOLOGY PROGRESS NOTE

Patient: Daniel Brooks
DOB: February 18, 1956
MRN: MRN-427615
Service date: August 2, 2024
Facility: Prairie Hope Cancer Hospital, 6300 Meadow Park Drive, Dallas, Texas 75235
Oncologist: Noor Hassan, MD

REASON FOR VISIT
Assessment before cycle 4 pembrolizumab, pemetrexed, and carboplatin for metastatic nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Daniel Brooks is a 68-year-old former electrician with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma involving the right upper lobe, mediastinal nodes, and a single left adrenal metastasis. Molecular testing showed no actionable EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET, RET, or NTRK alteration; PD-L1 was 30 percent. Treatment began May 31, 2024. He reports improved cough and exercise tolerance. Fatigue lasts four days after infusion. He has mild constipation controlled with polyethylene glycol and denies nausea, fever, rash, diarrhea, new dyspnea, hemoptysis, headache, weakness, or bone pain.

He lives with wife Margaret Brooks at 332 Prairie Wind Lane, Dallas, TX 75208. His mobile number is 214-555-0133 and email is daniel.brooks@example.test. Margaret Brooks can be reached at 214-555-0194. He quit smoking in 2018 after forty pack-years.

IMAGING AND TREATMENT HISTORY
Bronchoscopy biopsy on April 22, 2024 confirmed TTF-1-positive adenocarcinoma. PET-CT on May 2 showed the primary lesion, nodal disease, and left adrenal focus. Brain MRI on May 7 was negative. CT dated July 26 shows the primary mass decreased from 5.8 cm to 3.9 cm and the adrenal lesion from 2.1 cm to 1.2 cm, with no new disease.

MEDICATIONS
Cancer regimen as above; folic acid 1 mg daily; vitamin B12 per protocol; dexamethasone around pemetrexed; albuterol as needed; amlodipine 5 mg daily; polyethylene glycol as needed. No known allergies.

EXAM
ECOG 1. Temperature 36.8 C, blood pressure 134/76, pulse 90, oxygen saturation 96 percent, weight 79.6 kg. No distress. No adenopathy. Breath sounds mildly diminished at right apex without wheeze. Heart regular. Abdomen nontender. No edema, rash, clubbing, or focal neurologic deficit.

LABS
WBC 5.9, ANC 3.7, hemoglobin 10.5, platelets 238, creatinine 0.96, calcium 9.2, bilirubin 0.5, AST 25, ALT 29, TSH 1.9.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with partial radiographic response and acceptable toxicity. Proceed with cycle 4. After this cycle, transition to maintenance pemetrexed and pembrolizumab. Repeat CT in nine weeks. Continue folic acid and protocol vitamin B12. Call for fever, worsening breathing, severe rash, persistent diarrhea, or neurologic symptoms.

Daniel Brooks and Margaret Brooks reviewed the images and agreed with the plan. Return August 23, 2024. Signed by Noor Hassan, MD.

THORACIC MEDICAL ONCOLOGY FOLLOW-UP

Name: Daniel Brooks
Date of birth: 02/18/1956
Record number: MRN-427615
Date: August 23, 2024
Prairie Hope Cancer Hospital, Dallas infusion clinic
Provider: Noor Hassan, MD

INTERVAL HISTORY
Daniel Brooks returns for the first maintenance cycle of pemetrexed and pembrolizumab. Following cycle 4 on August 2, he had greater fatigue and reduced appetite for six days but remained independent. Cough is infrequent and nonproductive. He walked half a mile yesterday without stopping. There is no fever, chest pain, hemoptysis, resting dyspnea, diarrhea, rash, headache, or focal weakness. He notes mild swelling around both ankles late in the day that resolves overnight. He has not used albuterol this week.

His primary clinician, Grace Miller, NP, increased amlodipine to 10 mg on August 12. Daniel wonders whether this contributed to edema. Home blood pressure ranges from 124 to 138 systolic. Contact number and address remain 214-555-0133 and 332 Prairie Wind Lane.

CANCER STATUS
Stage IV right-upper-lobe adenocarcinoma with mediastinal and left adrenal involvement. Partial response documented July 26, 2024. Four induction cycles completed. No molecular target. Registry number SITE-CAN-0004.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive only for treatment-related fatigue, temporary anorexia, and evening ankle swelling. No oral ulcer, visual change, palpitations, vomiting, urinary symptom, joint inflammation, bruising, or sensory loss.

EXAMINATION
ECOG 1. Temperature 36.7 C, pulse 82, blood pressure 130/72, oxygen saturation 97 percent, weight 78.9 kg. Comfortable at rest. Oral mucosa moist. No cervical nodes. Lungs clear with mildly reduced right apical sounds. Heart regular. Abdomen soft. Trace symmetric ankle edema without calf tenderness. No rash. Neurologic examination nonfocal.

LABORATORY DATA
WBC 4.8, ANC 2.8, hemoglobin 9.8, platelets 205, creatinine 1.01, albumin 3.7, AST 23, ALT 26, bilirubin 0.4, TSH 2.2, free T4 1.0.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proceed with maintenance pemetrexed and pembrolizumab. Anemia is treatment related and does not require transfusion. Ankle edema is more consistent with increased amlodipine than cancer progression or thrombosis; Daniel will discuss dose adjustment with Grace Miller, NP. Continue folic acid and vitamin B12. CT chest and abdomen is scheduled October 4, 2024. Return September 13 for the next cycle.

Daniel Brooks understands immune-related warning symptoms and will call Prairie Hope at 214-555-0110 if they occur. Note signed by Noor Hassan, MD on August 23, 2024.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: Daniel Brooks
DOB: 02/18/1956
MRN: MRN-427615
Admission date: September 5, 2024
Discharge date: September 9, 2024
Facility: Prairie Hope Cancer Hospital, 6300 Meadow Park Drive, Dallas, TX 75235
Attending: Victor Stein, MD

PRINCIPAL PROBLEM
Community-acquired right lower-lobe pneumonia with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in a patient with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma.

OTHER ACTIVE PROBLEMS
